title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Staff
tiers.description: EMR Directors, Key Management Personnel, officers, employees and consultants. The insider trading prohibition, the blackout periods, board suspensions, the six month short-term trading ban and the section 11 hedge contract ban all apply to this tier.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: EMR Directors. Must obtain written approval from the Chairman for all dealings in EMR securities, must notify the Company Secretary within five business days for Listing Rule 3.19A and 3.19B purposes, and are prohibited from margin lending arrangements.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: The Chairman of the EMR board, who approves other Directors' and the Company Secretary's dealings and financial hardship blackout trading, and whose own dealings require written approval from the Managing Director.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Key Management Personnel other than the Company Secretary. Must obtain written approval from the Managing Director for all dealings and provide written confirmation to the Company Secretary once the dealing has taken place; prohibited from margin lending arrangements.

tiers.name: Company Secretary
tiers.description: The Company Secretary, treated with Directors for approval purposes: written advice to, and written approval from, the Chairman for all dealings in EMR securities.

tiers.name: Associated parties
tiers.description: A Staff member's spouse or partner, any dependent child, family company or family trust, and trusts of which Staff are trustees that invest in EMR securities. The policy applies equally to their dealings and Staff must so far as they are able prevent dealings at a time when they themselves are not free to deal.

definitions.hedging_definition: 'hedge contracts' or other forms of arrangements which may have the effect of fixing the value of, or return on, securities which form part of the incentive component of their remuneration or salary package (whether the securities are fully vested or not)

windows.start_anchor: 10 business days before the planned date for release of the relevant quarterly report for the calendar quarters ending 31 March and 30 September
windows.end_anchor: the business day after the day of release of the relevant quarterly report to ASX

windows.start_anchor: 10 business days before the planned date for release of the June quarterly report

windows.end_anchor: the business day after the release of the half year financial report to ASX for December

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The EMR board or the Managing Director may impose a suspension on the ability of Staff to trade at a time when trading might otherwise have been allowed, generally only in exceptional circumstances, and will endeavour to keep it to the shortest possible period. The policy does not say whether the existence or the reason for a suspension is confidential.

rules.detail: There is no derivatives rule. 'EMR securities' means shares, rights and options in EMR or associated companies, which is capable of covering an option over EMR shares written by a bank but does not clearly extend to a cash-settled OTC contract. Directors and the Company Secretary need the Chairman's written approval for all dealings in EMR securities, so an OTC put or call would on the wider reading require approval and be barred in blackout periods and suspensions.
rules.evidence: In the case of Directors and the Company Secretary, written advice must be given to, and written approval obtained from, the Chairman in respect of all dealings in EMR securities.

rules.detail: The policy contains no rule on derivatives, defines no term 'dealing', and imposes no approval requirement on Staff other than Directors, the Company Secretary and Key Management Personnel. For such Staff a derivative over EMR shares is constrained only by the insider trading prohibition, the blackout periods and, for incentive securities, the section 11 hedge contract ban.

Hedge contracts and other arrangements that may fix the value of or return on unvested incentive securities are prohibited for all Staff, covering both LTI plan securities and other securities issued as incentive remuneration such as sign-on or retention grants under employment agreements. No approval or waiver route is provided.
rules.evidence: EMR Staff are not permitted to enter into 'hedge contracts' or other forms of arrangements which may have the effect of fixing the value of, or return on, securities which form part of the incentive component of their remuneration or salary package (whether the securities are fully vested or not).

rules.detail: The ban follows the securities rather than their vesting state: incentive securities remain within it after they have fully vested. In practice any share traceable to an LTI grant or to incentive remuneration is permanently off limits for hedging, however long it has been held.
rules.evidence: securities which form part of the incentive component of their remuneration or salary package (whether the securities are fully vested or not). This not only includes EMR securities issued under the LTI plans but also other EMR securities issued by way of incentive remuneration

rules.detail: Shares that are not part of the incentive component of remuneration, such as shares bought on market or acquired in a placement or rights issue, fall outside the section 11 ban, which is expressed only by reference to incentive securities. Hedging such shares is not addressed anywhere in the policy.

For a Director or the Company Secretary, hedging non-incentive shares is not prohibited but, if it involves a dealing in EMR securities, it requires the Chairman's prior written approval (the Managing Director's, for the Chairman) and cannot occur in a blackout period or during a board suspension.
rules.evidence: In all cases, approval is to be given by the Chairman or Managing Director acting in accordance with this policy.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. Over incentive securities, a prepaid forward, collar or similar structure is an arrangement that may have the effect of fixing the value of or return on those securities and is prohibited by section 11. Over other securities it is not prohibited as such, but if the structure advances loaned monies supported by security over or transfer of EMR securities it becomes a margin lending arrangement barred to Directors and Key Management Personnel.
rules.evidence: not permitted to enter into 'hedge contracts' or other forms of arrangements which may have the effect of fixing the value of, or return on, securities which form part of the incentive component of their remuneration or salary package

rules.detail: Short selling is nowhere mentioned. The closest provision is the section 8 speculative trading ban, which is framed around purchase followed by sale rather than sale followed by purchase, although its parenthetical does capture a sale and subsequent purchase within six months.

Securities lending is not mentioned. A transfer of EMR securities is caught by the section 9 margin lending definition only where it supports loaned monies, which a stock loan for a fee would not ordinarily involve.

Contracts for difference are not mentioned. A CFD used to fix the return on incentive securities would be caught by the section 11 hedge contract ban, and a CFD entered by a Director or KMP might require approval as a dealing in EMR securities, but the instrument itself is not addressed.

An outright ban with no approval, hardship or exceptional circumstances route. The definition is deliberately wide and substance-based, catching any arrangement in the nature of loaned monies secured or otherwise supported by security over or transfer of EMR securities, regardless of form.
rules.evidence: Directors and Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into any dealing in EMR securities where such margin lending arrangements apply.

rules.detail: Key Management Personnel are subject to the same outright ban as Directors, with no distinction between vested and unvested securities and no waiver power.
rules.evidence: Margin lending refers to any arrangement which is in the nature of, or parties intend it to be in the nature of, loaned monies which are secured or are otherwise supported by a security over, or transfer of, EMR securities (regardless of the form the security or transfer takes).

rules.detail: Section 9 binds only Directors and Key Management Personnel. Officers, employees and consultants who are not KMP are not prohibited from margin lending and no notification or approval is required of them.

Granting security over, or transferring, EMR securities to support loaned monies is expressly within the margin lending definition and so prohibited for Directors and Key Management Personnel, whatever legal form the security or transfer takes. A charge or lien unconnected with borrowed money is not addressed.
rules.evidence: loaned monies which are secured or are otherwise supported by a security over, or transfer of, EMR securities (regardless of the form the security or transfer takes)

rules.detail: For Staff who are neither Directors nor Key Management Personnel, granting security over EMR securities is not addressed and requires no approval or notification.

Although headed 'Margin lending', section 9 operates as a general secured financing ban: it captures any arrangement in the nature of loaned monies secured or otherwise supported by EMR securities, so a bespoke bank facility secured on the shares, or a title-transfer collateral arrangement, is prohibited for Directors.
rules.evidence: Margin lending refers to any arrangement which is in the nature of, or parties intend it to be in the nature of, loaned monies which are secured or are otherwise supported by a security over, or transfer of, EMR securities (regardless of the form the security or transfer takes).

rules.detail: The same general secured financing ban applies to Key Management Personnel, and there is no exemption authority anywhere in the policy that could relieve it.
rules.evidence: Directors and Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into any dealing in EMR securities where such margin lending arrangements apply.

rules.detail: Six month intention-based test covering purchase with a view to selling or otherwise dealing, and expressly including a sale and subsequent purchase. Sales of shares converted on exercise of options or rights are excluded, and the Chairman or Managing Director may waive the prohibition in some circumstances.
rules.evidence: EMR's policy is also that Staff shall not engage in speculative trading whereby EMR securities are purchased with a view to selling or otherwise dealing (including by way of a sale and subsequent purchase) in those securities within a 6 month period.

In all cases, approval is to be given by the Chairman or Managing Director acting in accordance with this policy.

clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (written confirmation that the dealing has taken place)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: when the dealing has taken place; no deadline stated
clearance.evidence: In the case of Key Management Personnel (excluding the Company Secretary) written advice must be given to, and written approval obtained from, the Managing Director in respect of all dealings in EMR securities. Key Management Personnel are to provide written confirmation to the Company Secretary when the dealing has taken place.

Unless in possession of price sensitive information at the time of trading, Staff may generally trade EMR securities except: in a blackout referred to below, or if EMR suspends trading as referred to in section 6 above.

short_term.basis: from purchase, including a sale and subsequent purchase
carve_outs: the sale of shares that have been converted after exercising options or rights
circumstances waived by the Chairman of the EMR board or the Managing Director, for example the exercise of options or rights granted under the EMR Long-Term Incentive (LTI) Plans
short_term.evidence: However, the sale of shares that have been converted after exercising options or rights will not be regarded as short term trading.

exceptions.evidence: Only in cases of financial hardship can Staff trade EMR securities in a blackout period and in these circumstances written approval must be received from the Chairman.
an undertaking to accept, or acceptance of a takeover offer;
transfers in EMR securities already held by staff into a superannuation fund in which that person is a beneficiary;

dealings under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the shareholders of EMR, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan or a dividend or dividend reinvestment plan approved by the Board;
the cancellation, lapsing or surrender of an option or right under an LTI plan; and
an investment in, or trading in units of a fund (other than a fund only investing in EMR securities) where the assets of the fund are invested at the discretion of the third party.

exceptions.approver: Chairman of the EMR board or the Managing Director
exceptions.evidence: This prohibition on short-term trading may be waived by the Chairman of the EMR board or the Managing Director in some circumstances (e.g. exercise of options or rights granted under the EMR Long-Term Incentive (LTI) Plans).

external_documents: Employment agreements under which EMR securities are issued as incentive remuneration
exemption_authority: Limited and specific. The Chairman may give written approval for Staff to trade in a blackout period, but only in cases of financial hardship (section 7). The Chairman or the Managing Director may waive the six month short-term trading prohibition in some circumstances (section 8). The EMR board or Managing Director may impose or lift a trading suspension (section 6). There is no power anywhere to waive the section 9 margin lending prohibition or the section 11 hedge contract prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Margin lending refers to any arrangement which is in the nature of, or parties intend it to be in the nature of, loaned monies which are secured or are otherwise supported by a security over, or transfer of, EMR securities (regardless of the form the security or transfer takes).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The definition is drafted to defeat form-based structuring, so a bespoke bank loan, a limited recourse facility or a title transfer collateral arrangement supporting the collar is all margin lending and prohibited for Directors and KMP.

bespoke_clauses.topic: prohibition bites on the dealing, not just the loan
bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into any dealing in EMR securities where such margin lending arrangements apply.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: It is the dealing itself that is banned once a margin lending arrangement applies, so the collar legs and the pledge fall together with the loan rather than being severable from it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: EMR Staff are not permitted to enter into 'hedge contracts' or other forms of arrangements which may have the effect of fixing the value of, or return on, securities which form part of the incentive component of their remuneration or salary package (whether the securities are fully vested or not).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any share traceable to an LTI grant or to incentive remuneration can never be collared, however long ago it vested, so only shares bought or subscribed for independently are candidates.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no general hedging, derivatives or short selling prohibition; section 11 is confined to incentive securities and section 9 to margin lending.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An unfunded collar over shares that a Director bought on market is not prohibited, and would need only the Chairman's written approval outside a blackout period; the funding leg is what makes the structure impossible.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In all cases, approval is to be given by the Chairman or Managing Director acting in accordance with this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no stated validity period, response time, revocation right or condition-imposing power, so the parties must agree contractually how long an approval is treated as good for.

bespoke_clauses.clause: there may be occasions when the EMR board imposes a suspension on the ability of Staff to trade at a time when trading might otherwise have been allowed ... If a suspension occurs, Staff must not trade while the suspension is in force.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An ad hoc suspension can block entry, roll, unwind or physical settlement at any time, and only financial hardship approval by the Chairman relieves a blackout, not a suspension.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the blackout period starts 10 business days before the planned date for release of the relevant quarterly report ... and ends on the business day after the day of release
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: As a quarterly reporting explorer EMR has four blackout periods a year rather than two, materially narrowing the windows in which a collar could be entered or unwound.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Staff shall not engage in speculative trading whereby EMR securities are purchased with a view to selling or otherwise dealing (including by way of a sale and subsequent purchase) in those securities within a 6 month period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Tenor should exceed six months, and shares recently acquired should not be collared, since the arrangement could be read as purchase with a view to otherwise dealing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy applies equally to any dealings in EMR securities by a Staff's spouse, partner or by or on behalf of any dependent child, family company or family trust.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Placing the shares, the pledge or the derivative in a family company or trust does not avoid the margin lending or hedge contract prohibitions.

summary: A funded collar is not possible for an EMR Director or Key Management Personnel, because the funding leg is prohibited. Section 9 defines margin lending in substance rather than form, as any arrangement in the nature of loaned monies secured or otherwise supported by a security over, or transfer of, EMR securities regardless of the form the security or transfer takes, and bars Directors and KMP from entering into any dealing in EMR securities where such an arrangement applies, with no waiver power. The derivative legs are separately impossible over any share that forms part of the incentive component of remuneration, since section 11 bans hedge contracts and arrangements fixing the value of or return on those securities whether or not they have fully vested. An unfunded collar over shares acquired independently of incentive remuneration is not prohibited and would need only the Chairman's prior written approval (the Managing Director's, for the Chairman), taken outside the four quarterly blackout periods and any board suspension, with notification to the Company Secretary within five business days and a tenor beyond the six month speculative trading rule. Staff who are neither Directors nor KMP are outside section 9 altogether, but they are not the relevant client group.
